findings.reason: without the s2→s1 edge the queue dispatches the deletion node against an unclassified tree, and a module §1 finds reached could be deleted on a stale guess.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares `{s3:[s1], s4:[s1], s5:[s3,s4], s6:[s5]}` and leaves `s2` unconstrained, yet §2 says "`contour_tree_layout.py` is also unreached ... §1 decides it" and its five deletions take their authority from §2's source review plus §1's classification; the deletion node would therefore be admitted while the census that defines its scope is still unlanded

findings.reason: the census is the authority every later node reads, and a set that omits `apps/` lets a live consumer of a `machine_*` module fall between §1's census and §3/§4's package-scoped gates.
findings.text: §1 enumerates importers only under `nova/`, `scripts/` and `benchmarks/`, but `apps/playable/machines.py:151` imports `nova.imas.machine_artifact` and resolves a machine description through it; §2's scan does include `apps/`, while §3 and §4 constrain only "no module left in the nova package", so this out-of-package consumer is neither recorded nor owned and breaks when the module moves or is generalised

findings.reason: a node acting on "three places" removes `packages/nova-cocos` and leaves `imas-alambic` and nova's own workspace and dependency declarations resolving against a missing package, the failure §5 says the landing beat exists to prevent.
findings.text: the plan says imas-ambix "imports the algebra from `nova_cocos` in three places" and that "its dependency" moves in the same landing beat, but the measured set is four source sites (`imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py:28`, `imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py:26`, `tests/data/test_cocos_convention.py:11`, `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/cocos.py:21`), with `packages/imas-alambic/pyproject.toml:31` declaring `nova-cocos` as its own dependency. nova also still declares it at `pyproject.toml:41` and lists it in `[tool.uv.workspace] members` (line 168), and imas-ambix's `uv.lock` carries two dependents on the package — none of which the removal's done-when covers

findings.reason: a census destination with no owning node produces a record whose decision is never executed, so the plan should either narrow the destination vocabulary to what §2–§4 land or name the node that lands the remainder.
findings.text: §1 assigns every census row one of four destinations (`stays in nova`, `moves to the ingest member`, `generalised into a generic module`, `deleted`), but no node lands "generalised into a generic module" or "deleted" for any row outside §2's five named files; §2 deletes five specific modules and §3/§4 only move `mast_*`, `diiid_*` and `machine_*` rows
